sections.html:
Taunton is the seat of Bristol County in southeastern Massachusetts, on the Taunton River about 10 miles north of Mount Hope Bay. The 2020 census counted 59,408 residents, third in the county behind New Bedford and Fall River. By area, at 48.4 square miles, it ranks third in the state after Boston and Barnstable.

That size means a Taunton address can be a downtown street near the Green, a lakeside lot or a wooded parcel near the industrial park in the north. ZIP codes are 02780 and 02718 (East Taunton). Tell buyers which part of the city your house is in, because the choices are so different.

Colonists settled Taunton in the late 1630s, and it was incorporated as a town on September 3, 1639, making it one of the oldest towns in the country. It became a city in 1864. Its original boundaries took in land that is now Norton, Easton, Mansfield, Dighton, Raynham, Berkley and Lakeville.

In the 1800s the city earned the name Silver City because companies such as Reed & Barton, F. B. Rogers and Poole Silver made silverware here. Since December 1914 a large December light display on Taunton Green has added the nickname Christmas City. Older neighborhoods carry that history in their houses, so expect buyers to ask about updates.

Taunton is the highway hub of southeastern Massachusetts. U.S. 44, Route 138 and Route 140 meet at the Green, Route 24 meets Route 140 near East Taunton, and Interstate 495 runs through the north.

One MBTA Commuter Rail stop, East Taunton station, serves the city. A proposed second phase of the South Coast Rail project would add a stop near downtown on Dean Street. GATRA runs local buses, and the city has a municipal airport for small aircraft. The nearest national airline service is T.F. Green Airport in Rhode Island, and the nearest international flights leave from Logan in Boston.

Taunton is built around a river, with ponds, low ground and two state parks, Massasoit State Park in East Taunton and Watson Pond State Park in the north. A buyer for a lot near water may ask about flood zones and drainage. FEMA maps and the local conservation office hold that information, so check them for your own parcel.

Winter snow mostly falls from December through March. Roof, gutters and heating records are standard inspection topics, and a short list of dates for the roof, heating and wiring helps buyers of older houses.

Downtown centers on Taunton Green, a former militia training ground with a fountain at its center. Nearby are the public library, which opened in 1903, the Old Colony Historical Society and the Bristol County Superior Courthouse, with a trial court complex finished in 2011.

The economy has shifted from silversmithing and shipbuilding toward manufacturing and industrial parks, with the Myles Standish Industrial Park beside Interstate 495 as the main one. The Silver City Galleria mall closed on February 29, 2020 and was demolished on May 9, 2021, which reshaped retail in the area. People who sold or relocated for jobs sometimes need a fast, simple sale.

Taunton operates nine public elementary schools, three middle schools (Benjamin A. Friedman, Joseph H. Martin and John F. Parker) and Taunton High School. Family buyers often start with the school list, so have it ready for a listing or a private sale.

The fire department must issue a certificate of compliance for the home's smoke and carbon monoxide alarms before a Taunton sale can close. State guidance is to phone as soon as the closing is set, and the inspection comes with a local fee.

The alarms you need depend on the year of construction and the last building permit. Alarms with no manufacture date count as expired, and old battery units give way to sealed ten-year photoelectric models with a hush button.

Most Massachusetts deeds are recorded land filed at the county Registry of Deeds, and masslandrecords.com lets you search the records. Attorneys take part in most closings, so line up yours early.

sections.h2: Which selling path fits a Taunton owner?
sections.html:
• Listing: the widest buyer pool, with prep, showings and financing delays
  • Private sale: saves fees, adds paperwork and negotiation
  • Cash as-is: a simpler close, with an offer that reflects condition

Owners with inherited houses, vacant houses or deferred repairs often pick cash to avoid showings and repair requests. In a cash sale, you describe the house, the buyer reviews the address, condition and any liens or taxes, and you get an offer. If you accept, a title company or attorney handles the paperwork, and closing follows your timeline. Declining is always an option.

Whichever route you pick, compare the net result after fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. Nobody can promise a price before reviewing the property.

sections.h2: From first call to closing day
sections.html:
1. Gather your tax bill, repair receipts, alarm dates and any records for past work.
  2. Decide between a listing, a private sale and a cash offer based on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.
  3. Book the fire department visit for the alarm certificate once a closing date exists.
  4. Pick an attorney or title company to handle the deed and the payoff of any mortgage.
  5. Review the written offer and the contract, then sign.
  6. Close, record the deed and hand over the keys.

Timelines vary with title questions and the buyer. A cash sale is shorter mostly because no lender is involved and nobody has to schedule an appraisal or repair negotiation. A listing can take longer, since you wait for showings and for a buyer's financing to clear.

sections.h2: Older houses and what to disclose
sections.html:
Taunton has houses from the colonial era to modern buildings, and age is the first thing a buyer prices in. If a lot sits near a pond, river or low ground, say so and share any drainage work you have done. If tenants live there, hand over the lease early. If the house sat vacant after an inheritance, note what has been shut off or repaired.

Describing problems in writing protects you and keeps surprises out of the inspection. A cash buyer usually accepts the condition as it stands, so the same honesty simply sets a fair price faster.

Ask for the offer in writing and read who pays which closing cost. Confirm that the buyer can show proof of funds. Check what happens to any unpaid taxes or liens, which are normally settled out of your proceeds at closing. Gather your tax bill, repair receipts and alarm dates in one folder so questions get quick answers.

faqs.q: What county is Taunton, MA in?
faqs.a: Taunton is in Bristol County and serves as the county seat.
Taunton covers 48.4 square miles and had 59,408 residents in 2020, which makes it the third-largest city by area in Massachusetts.

faqs.q: Is there a commuter train in Taunton?
faqs.a: Yes, East Taunton station on the MBTA Commuter Rail. A proposed South Coast Rail phase would add a stop near downtown on Dean Street.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell in Taunton?
faqs.a: Yes. The department must certify that your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the sale rules. Schedule it once you have a closing date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Taunton house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as they are, though the offer reflects the repairs needed.
